tools.name: wi_webinar
tools.description: Plan, write and set up a webinar from a chat, and answer questions about WebinarIgnition. It picks a topic, produces the title, the invitation emails, the reminders and the registration page, and prepares the live, automated or evergreen room on the user's own WordPress site. tools.name: wi_webinar_delete
tools.description: Delete or replace something on the connected WordPress site — irreversible. Runs only an ability that is verified as destructive: delete a campaign, a webhook, registrants (single or all), the logs, the attendee questions, or the HC import that replaces a campaign. Writes abilities are not run here;

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.webinarignition.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: wi_webinar · Public sink: wi_webinar_delete · Destructive: wi_webinar, wi_webinar_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: wi_webinar · Public sink: wi_webinar_delete · Destructive: wi_webinar, wi_webinar_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
